text:
If you're heading out for sunset, tonight starts on a pleasant note: clear and comfortable now, with the sun setting at 7:31. Clouds will thicken afterward, and a few showers could arrive after 3am. It'll stay mild, with a low around 60, light winds, and very little lake chop.

Tomorrow is the less certain call. The official forecast puts us near 74 with mostly cloudy skies and a 50% chance of showers, but the models spread from around 70 to 78 and from a few showers to a much wetter day. I’d lean toward a cool, occasionally showery Tuesday rather than a washout, but keep the rain jacket handy. The lake should stay quiet, with waves a foot or less, so early waterfront plans are workable, just don't count on a bright day.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) — Happy Monday, our Monday morning started with patchy dense fog early on, but we find more sunshine into this afternoon and evening. While most of us see a good deal of sunshine, there could be more cloud cover and a few spotty showers the further west you look, in particular out towards St. Lawrence County. High temperatures for the day climb back into the mid and upper 70s this afternoon. Clouds return for most tonight, as lows dip into the 50s and lower 60s by early Tuesday morning.
